def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ T : Set Form, Def14 T (K (ex 1 Def16)) → Def14 T (K (ex 1 (and Def17 (neg (K Def17)))))
a_raw: {"translation":"Write R(a,b) for the atom with relation symbol 0 and variable arguments a and b. Target is the following proposition: for every set T of formulas, if K(∃y ∀x (K(¬R(x,x)) ↔ R(y,x))) is derivable from T, then K(∃y (¬R(y,y) ∧ ¬K(¬R(y,y)))) is derivable from that same T. Here y is variable 1 and x is variable 0. In both formulas the outer K covers the whole existential formula; no particular witness is required. There is no restriction on T. Derivability means obtainability by modus ponens from members of T and the Def13 axioms: the latter are Def11 formulas prefixed by zero or more universal quantifiers, or K applied to such a prefixed formula."}
translation: Write R(a,b) for the atom with relation symbol 0 and variable arguments a and b. Target is the following proposition: for every set T of formulas, if K(∃y ∀x (K(¬R(x,x)) ↔ R(y,x))) is derivable from T, then K(∃y (¬R(y,y) ∧ ¬K(¬R(y,y)))) is derivable from that same T. Here y is variable 1 and x is variable 0. In both formulas the outer K covers the whole existential formula; no particular witness is required. There is no restriction on T. Derivability means obtainability by modus ponens from members of T and the Def13 axioms: the latter are Def11 formulas prefixed by zero or more universal quantifiers, or K applied to such a prefixed formula.

judgement.summary: For the stated instance, Lean takes U(e,x) = R(e,x) and p(x) = q(x) = ¬R(x,x), as in the diagonal choice in the proof. It says that if T derives a) with K prefixed to the whole existential formula, then the same T derives b) with K prefixed in exactly the same way.
